row.notes: In Sess_Ai_BuildVehicleRecords: mov rax,[rcx+0x108], the first instruction after the car name hash call (call 0x1405ed3a0 at 0x1438a3c8c; mov rcx,r13 / mov r13,rax at 0x1438a3c91/94). Here r13 = the car name hash, rcx = the manager, [rsp+0x60] = the vehicle index. The group walk that follows compares [node+0x20] with r13 in each group's map ([[group]+8] is the std::map head: +0 left/leftmost, +8 root, node left +0, right +0x10, isnil byte +0x19, key +0x20). Core's guard replaces r13 with the key of group 0's leftmost node when group 0 lacks the hash, so the unmodified code finds a node and builds a full record at the vehicle's slot; the records at [mgr+0x128] are indexed by vehicle slot.

verify.notes: V8616 sigcheck hits=1 match=0x1438a3c91 target=0x1438a3c97 (mov rax,[rcx+0x108]). Disassembled: call 0x1405ed3a0 returns the hash in rax, 0x1438a3c91 mov rcx,r13 (manager, loaded from param at prologue and [rsp+0x30]) and 0x1438a3c94 mov r13,rax, so at the site r13=hash, rcx=manager, [rsp+0x60] is stored later at 0x1438a3c5c before the call so already holds the index. No jump or call targets 0x1438a3c98-0x1438a3c9e (grepped the function disassembly) so the 7-byte window is clean. r13 is consumed only as the hash: lower_bound at 0x1438a3d14 (cmp [node+0x20],r13; cmovae takes left=+0 else right=+0x10), equality check at 0x1438a3d3c and the nested lookup at 0x1438a3e5c/61; r13 is rewritten as a temp afterwards. Replacing it with the group 0 leftmost key makes group 0 hit, so the unmodified code builds a normal record in the vehicle's slot; later groups that lack it just end the walk with one node.
